text:
The most expensive message in a services business is the quote that never gets a follow-up.

Interiors, travel, events, solar, renovation: someone asks for a price, you spend an hour on the quote, you send it, and then silence.

Most owners don't follow up because it feels pushy. So the quote dies, even when the customer was simply busy.

A follow-up that doesn't feel pushy:
→ Day 2: answer a question they probably have ("Most clients ask about the timeline. Here's ours.")
→ Day 5: offer a smaller first step (a site visit, a sample, a call)
→ Day 10: one last message that makes it easy to say no: "Should I close this for now?"

That last line gets more replies than any discount, because it lets people be honest.

Three messages. Write them once, and send them on schedule every time.
